subject: Physics
title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
summary: A moving charge (current) produces a magnetic field B around it (Oersted). The Biot–Savart law gives the field of a current element; for symmetric cases (long wire, solenoid, toroid) Ampere's circuital law is quicker.

A magnetic field exerts force on a moving charge: F = q(v × B). This force is always perpendicular to velocity, so speed doesn't change and no work is done — only the direction turns (circle or helix). With both E and B, the Lorentz force is F = q(E + v × B).
A current-carrying wire feels F = I(L × B). Two parallel wires attract if currents are in the same direction and repel if opposite; this gave the definition of the ampere.

A current loop is a magnetic dipole (m = NIA); in a uniform field the net force is zero but there is a torque τ = m × B. This is the principle of the moving coil galvanometer, which becomes an ammeter with a small parallel resistance (shunt) and a voltmeter with a large series resistance.

formulas.name: Biot–Savart law
formulas.formula: dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂ / r² = (μ₀/4π) I dl sin θ / r²
formulas.when: Field of a wire of any shape (adding small pieces).
formulas.note: r points from the element to the point; θ is between dl (along the current) and r.

formulas.name: Field at centre of circular loop
formulas.formula: B = μ₀NI / 2R;   arc (angle φ radian): B = μ₀Iφ / 4πR
formulas.when: Centre of a circular coil or arc.
formulas.mistake: Put φ in radians, not degrees.

formulas.name: Field on axis of circular loop
formulas.formula: B = μ₀NIR² / [2(R² + x²)^{3/2}];   x ≫ R: B ≈ μ₀m / 2πx³
formulas.when: Point on the axis of a coil.
formulas.mistake: Putting x = 0 should give the centre formula — check it.

formulas.name: Straight wire
formulas.formula: Finite: B = (μ₀I/4πd)(sin φ₁ + sin φ₂);   infinite: B = μ₀I / 2πd;   opposite the end of a semi-infinite wire: μ₀I/4πd
formulas.when: Field at distance d from a straight wire.
formulas.mistake: The angles are measured from the perpendicular, not along the wire.

formulas.name: Ampere's circuital law
formulas.when: Symmetric cases: long wire, solenoid, toroid, thick wire.
formulas.mistake: Don't count currents outside the loop in I_enclosed.

formulas.name: Thick (solid) wire, radius R
formulas.formula: Inside (r < R): B = μ₀Ir / 2πR²;   outside: B = μ₀I / 2πr
formulas.note: Inside, the field INCREASES with r and is maximum at the surface.

formulas.name: Solenoid and toroid
formulas.formula: Long solenoid inside: B = μ₀nI (n = turns per metre), at the end μ₀nI/2;   toroid: B = μ₀NI / 2πr
formulas.mistake: n is turns per METRE, not total turns.

formulas.name: Force on moving charge (Lorentz)
formulas.formula: F = q(v × B);   |F| = qvB sin θ;   with E also: F = q(E + v × B)
formulas.note: For an electron (negative) the direction is reversed — flip after using the hand rule.

formulas.name: Circular path in uniform B
formulas.formula: r = mv/qB = p/qB = √(2mK)/qB;   T = 2πm/qB;   f = qB/2πm
formulas.mistake: The time period does NOT depend on speed (the cyclotron is based on this).

formulas.name: Helical path
formulas.formula: v at angle θ to B: radius = mv sin θ / qB;   pitch = 2πm v cos θ / qB
formulas.mistake: cos θ in the pitch, sin θ in the radius — don't swap them.

formulas.name: Velocity selector
formulas.formula: E and B perpendicular: undeflected when v = E/B
formulas.mistake: Only for that speed; mass and charge don't matter.

formulas.name: Force on current-carrying wire
formulas.formula: F = I(L × B);   |F| = BIL sin θ;   any closed loop in uniform B: F_net = 0
formulas.note: The force on a curved wire equals that on the straight line joining its ends.

formulas.name: Force between parallel wires
formulas.formula: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂ / 2πd;   same direction attract, opposite repel
formulas.note: Opposite of electric charges: here 'like' currents attract.

formulas.name: Magnetic dipole moment and torque
formulas.formula: m = NIA (direction by right-hand rule);   τ = m × B, |τ| = NIAB sin θ;   U = −m·B
formulas.mistake: Measure θ from the normal (m), not from the PLANE of the loop.

formulas.name: Moving coil galvanometer
formulas.formula: NIAB = kφ ⇒ φ = (NAB/k) I;   current sensitivity φ/I = NAB/k;   voltage sensitivity φ/V = NAB/(kR_G)
formulas.mistake: More turns raise current sensitivity but not necessarily voltage sensitivity (R also grows).

formulas.name: Galvanometer → ammeter / voltmeter
formulas.formula: Ammeter: shunt S = I_g G / (I − I_g) in parallel.   Voltmeter: R = V/I_g − G in series
formulas.mistake: An ammeter has very low resistance, a voltmeter very high — connecting them the wrong way can burn the meter.

examples.title: Force and radius for an electron
examples.problem: An electron moves at 2 × 10⁶ m/s perpendicular to B = 0.5 T. Force and radius of the circle? (m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg)

examples.title: Cyclotron frequency
examples.problem: A proton circles in B = 1 T. Frequency? (m_p = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)
examples.solution: f = qB/2πm = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (2π × 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷) ≈ 1.52 × 10⁷ Hz — independent of speed.

examples.title: Force between parallel wires

examples.title: Torque on a coil
examples.problem: 50 turns, area 0.02 m², current 1 A, B = 0.2 T; the coil's normal is at 30° to B. Magnetic moment and torque?

examples.title: Galvanometer to ammeter and voltmeter
examples.problem: G = 50 Ω, full-scale I_g = 5 mA. Make (a) a 0–5 A ammeter (b) a 0–10 V voltmeter.
examples.solution: (a) S = I_g G/(I − I_g) = 0.005 × 50/4.995 ≈ 0.05 Ω in parallel. (b) R = V/I_g − G = 2000 − 50 = 1950 Ω in series.

topics.title: Oersted's experiment
topics.explain: A compass needle near a current-carrying wire deflects — current produces a magnetic field. Reversing the current reverses the deflection. Field lines are concentric circles around the wire.

topics.title: Direction rules
topics.explain: Right-hand thumb rule: thumb along current, fingers give B (long wire). For a loop/solenoid, curl fingers with the current and the thumb gives B (north). For force use the cross product in F = q(v × B) or Fleming's left-hand rule.

topics.title: Applications of Biot–Savart
topics.explain: Field at the centre and on the axis of a circular loop, field of an arc, finite wire. For an element, the field is proportional to current and inversely proportional to distance squared.

topics.title: Applications of Ampere's law
topics.explain: Infinite wire (B ∝ 1/r), inside a solid wire (B ∝ r), solenoid (uniform μ₀nI inside, ≈ 0 outside), toroid (μ₀NI/2πr inside, zero outside). Choose an Amperian loop where B is constant and parallel to dl.

topics.title: Motion of charges in E and B
topics.explain: Only B: circle (v ⊥ B), helix (oblique), straight line (v ∥ B, zero force). The magnetic force does no work ⇒ KE stays constant. Crossed E and B: velocity selector. A cyclotron uses f = qB/2πm to accelerate charges repeatedly.

topics.title: Definition of ampere
topics.explain: If two infinitely long parallel wires 1 m apart carry equal currents and the force between them is 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre, each current is 1 ampere. (Since 2019 the SI ampere is defined through the elementary charge e, but this relation remains true.)

topics.title: Current loop as a magnetic dipole
topics.explain: A loop behaves like a small bar magnet: m = NIA, one face north and one south. Far away its field is dipole-like (1/r³). In a uniform field the net force is zero and the torque m × B tends to align m with B.

topics.title: Moving coil galvanometer
topics.explain: The coil sits in a radial magnetic field (concave poles + soft iron core) ⇒ sin θ = 1 in every position, so deflection is proportional to current (linear scale). A spring provides restoring torque kφ. To raise sensitivity increase N, B, A or decrease k.

ratta: Loop centre μ₀NI/2R;  wire μ₀I/2πd;  solenoid μ₀nI.
m = NIA;  τ = mB sin θ;  U = −mB cos θ.
Shunt S = I_g G/(I − I_g);  series R = V/I_g − G.
